title: Change-gated eval rubric and confidence calibration
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: Implement a change-gated evaluation and scoring pipeline that ties model/config changes to calibrated quality signals. We want deterministic, actionable alerts for quality regressions while minimizing false positives and compute cost.

Scope: (1) Define a canonical rubric mapping across our major eval suites (summarization, dialogue, instruction-following, embeddings) with standardized granularity and per-criterion directions; (2) Integrate an LLM-as-judge ensemble that returns both a score and a calibrated confidence for each judgment; (3) Add a calibration layer (temperature + isotonic calibration) measured against a small human-labeled seed; (4) Wire the pipeline to CI/PR flows so any model/config change triggers targeted re-evals and gating.

Success criteria:
- CI gate flags regressions with precision >= 85% on historical change set and recall >= 90% for >1.0 point mean-opinion delta on critical rubrics.
- Per-change compute overhead limited to <= 30% of current nightly eval budget via targeted test selection.
- Clear runbook for triage and auto-remediation (canary, rollback, or manual review) in place.

Non-goals: Full re-annotation of datasets; global rebaseline for every tiny config tweak.

Design decisions so far: We will compute a Signal Stability Score (SSS) per change: SSS = mean(delta * calibrated_confidence) / sqrt(variance + epsilon). SSS thresholds: soft-warning at 0.6, hard-block at 1.2 (tunable after initial calibration). Statistical validation uses bootstrap resampling to estimate CIs and report p-values; we will require both absolute effect size and significance for a hard-block.

Data & privacy: Use anonymized examples for hosted evals; for Private deployments, run the same pipeline locally (customer-managed) — feature flags will allow differing thresholds.

Artifacts: Confluence draft with rubric matrix: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/EVALS/Change-Gated-Rubric (internal); initial GitHub PR for the evaluator service: https://github.com/redwood-inference/evals/pull/482; dashboard prototype: https://grafana.redwood.com/d/evals/change-gated (internal).
comments: 2026-02-14 - Kickoff meeting: aligned on metrics, Ravi will own engineering integration, Maya will own rubric consolidation. Action: eng to provide CI hook spec by 2026-02-21.

2026-02-21 - ENG update: CI hook spec posted in #infra-evals. Proposed flow: on PR to models or config, compute diff against pinned baseline, select targeted test shard, run LLM-judge ensemble at n=3, emit SSS and p-value. (See PR draft: https://github.com/redwood-inference/evals/pull/482).

2026-02-28 - PM decision: Use ensemble of 3 judge models of different families to reduce judge-model bias. Agreed to add isotonic calibration against human seed set of 500 examples per task. Estimated extra compute ~22% of nightly budget.
2026-03-04 - Design feedback from K. Ortiz: request explicit failure modes in UI for analysts (why flagged, which rubric dimension, top counterexamples). Added label request 'explainable-flag'.

2026-03-08 - ENG note: implemented prototype that returns per-utterance score + confidence and a short rationale string. Hooked to Grafana dashboard for visual review. Example run: model v2.3 -> SSS=1.35, p=0.004 => flagged as hard-block in staging.
